name: claude-code-video-toolkit
description: AI-native video production workspace for Claude Code

remotion-official.description: Official Remotion framework knowledge (synced weekly from remotion-dev/skills `skills/remotion-best-practices/` — router skill embedding markup, maps, captions, render, saas, studio, docs, upgrade sub-skills)

remotion.description: Toolkit-specific Remotion patterns — custom transitions, shared components, conventions, motion craft

video-design.description: Visual design for videos: colour fields by act (two or three, ordered by lightness), one data accent, five type steps, two-line titles, chart and layout rules; a design.md handoff any design source can fill; a contact-sheet critique with a weighted score and caps
video-design.note: Takes direction from the project's design source (designSources) or the brand alone. Parts adapted from taste-skill (MIT).

elevenlabs.description: ElevenLabs audio - TTS, voice cloning, music, SFX

ffmpeg.description: FFmpeg video/audio processing for Remotion assets

playwright-recording.description: Playwright browser recording for demo videos

qwen-edit.description: AI image editing prompting patterns and best practices for Qwen-Image (Edit-2511 by default, 2.1 as a non-commercial Modal opt-in)

runpod.description: Cloud GPU setup, Docker images, endpoint management, troubleshooting

acestep.description: AI music generation — prompt engineering, scene presets, lyrics formatting, video production integration

ltx2.description: AI video generation — prompting guide, parameters, video production use cases (b-roll, animated slides, portraits); LTX-2.5 as a deploy-time opt-in

moviepy.description: Python video composition with moviepy 2.x — overlaying text on LTX-2/SadTalker output, single-file build.py video projects

ideogram4.description: Prompting patterns for Ideogram 4 text-to-image — structured JSON captions for best-in-class in-image text, color-palette and bounding-box layout control (title cards, thumbnails, CTAs)
ideogram4.note: Skill teaches the JSON caption format; Claude is the magic-prompt expander. Tool: tools/ideogram4.py. Hosted paid API (commercial license, ~$0.03–0.10/img); not self-hosted. Needs IDEOGRAM_API_KEY. Ideogram 4.5 is an opt-in (--model 4.5, v2 API) that reads the same captions; run live, near-perfect with JSON captions, garbled filler text with plain prompts.

synthetic-ui-demo.description: Product demo and release-notes videos with no screen recording: rebuild the app's screens as static React from its source, drive them with a scripted cursor and camera (Stage + Cursor)
synthetic-ui-demo.note: Reference builds: examples/ds-free-schedule-demo (one flow) and examples/ds-release-649 (a whole release). Product screen kits stay in the project, not lib.

parody-short.description: Comedy shorts about a group's own life (a team, club, class or family) or a shared topic, in a borrowed genre, starring the group's animated photos or an invented cast: mining the group's context for in-jokes, mapping genre beats onto the event, costume (image_edit) then animate and extend (LTX, ltx_extend.py) the cast, sound placed with sync_check.py, vertical cuts and brand editions, and the affection and privacy rules
parody-short.note: Learned on three internal videos starring real colleagues (an 80s action-show release intro, a Halloween creature feature, a Dickens Christmas ad) and two public shorts with an invented cast (a horror trailer, a wildlife documentary), 2026-11

video-toolkit.description: Agent-facing skill for any runtime (OpenClaw, Codex, Hermes, a run_tool loop, MCP clients): a routes table first (which template, skill and example fits what the user asks, and whether it runs as a job or is a build; video_job.py catalog lists them from this registry), then the estimate -> submit -> poll status -> result flow of tools/video_job.py first, then the individual tools with current defaults (SoulX, Ideogram for text, qc.py before delivery, --max-wpm)
video-toolkit.audience: agents other than Claude Code; keeps the metadata.openclaw frontmatter so OpenClaw loads it
video-toolkit.note: Was skills/openclaw-video-toolkit (OpenClaw-only paths and yieldMs polling) until 2026-10-31

youtube-stats.description: Reading how published videos do (youtube_stats.py): what each metric means for a Short vs a long video, the Analytics scope step, and what has worked on Shorts so far, kept as findings rather than numbers

blender.description: 3D scenes, character acting and product shots from a shot spec, as a film, as clips for any build, or as elements of a Remotion video: spec format, the cast schema (build, face, hair, clothes, accessories, seed, a character file per kit), sets (desk_room, desk, studio with phone, card and model props), shot types and camera moves, acting verbs, narration cues, the check/contact-sheet loop, BlenderClip compositing, brief-to-beats shot grammar, Blender Python vs MCP, Blender 5 gotchas

designSources._note: Plug in your own design skill, or use ours. Design skills give video-design its direction; they're installed by the user from their own repos, never copied into the toolkit. 'ours' is the toolkit's own: video-design's act palettes and rules with the project's brand, nothing to install. /design and /scene-review offer the installed ones plus ours; the project's choice is project.json design.source. List one by opening an issue (see .claude/skills/video-design/sources.md).

ours.description: The toolkit's own: video-design's act palettes (brand + bone + black, graphite, paper, loud two-act) and rules with the project's brand; nothing to install

taste-skill.description: Dealt directions and palettes from 247 studied sites, measured house rules, a juror's critique with caps

frontend-design.description: Anthropic's general visual direction for interfaces; written for web pages, so its effects (gradient meshes, glows) are turned down for video

video.description: Video projects - list, resume, or create new

brand.description: Brand profiles - list, edit, or create new

template.description: List available templates and their features

skills.description: List installed skills or create new ones

record-demo.description: Guided Playwright recording with interactive or script mode

generate-voiceover.description: Generate TTS voiceover using ElevenLabs or Qwen3-TTS, with optional burned captions

contribute.description: Share improvements - issues, PRs, skills, templates, and videos you made

scene-review.description: Scene-by-scene review in Remotion Studio before voiceover

design.description: Set a video's design direction (design.md) from a design source, refine a scene, or critique the render

versions.description: Check dependency versions and toolkit updates

redub.description: Redub video with a different voice (transcribe + TTS)

voice-clone.description: Record, test, and save a cloned voice to a brand profile

setup.description: First-time toolkit setup - cloud GPU, file transfer, voice, and prerequisites

thumbnail.description: Generate a 1280x720 YouTube thumbnail for a project - hook phrase + brand colours as an Ideogram 4 JSON caption, text checked, written to out/thumbnail.png for /publish

publish.description: Publish a finished video to YouTube - auto-fills metadata and thumbnail (from /thumbnail) from project.json, then uploads; Shorts via tools/cutdown.py first

voiceover.description: Generate TTS voiceovers using ElevenLabs, Qwen3-TTS, or 60db

options.stability: Voice stability 0-1 (unified scale; auto-converted to 0-100 for 60db)
options.model: ElevenLabs: eleven_multilingual_v2 (default), eleven_flash_v2_5, eleven_v3, eleven_v4 (Text to Dialogue API; stability+similarity only, chunked >2,000 chars). Deprecated eleven_turbo_v2_5 is accepted with a warning and sent as eleven_flash_v2_5
options.pacingQC: results include wpm + pacing label (fast/slow/ok); --max-wpm clamps fast takes with pitch-preserving atempo (floor 0.85x, --min-tempo lowers it to 0.7x)

music_gen.description: AI music generation using ACE-Step 1.5 (text-to-music, cover, stem extraction, repainting, continuation). Modal: XL Turbo 4B (acestep-v15-xl-turbo, ACE-Step-1.5 v0.1.8); RunPod: 2B turbo

options.preset: Scene preset (corporate-bg, upbeat-tech, ambient, dramatic, tension, hopeful, cta, lofi)
options.thinking: Enable 5Hz LM thinking mode (default for acemusic)
options.repaint: Repaint mode: regenerate a time segment (acemusic only)
options.extract: Stem extraction (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other)

sfx_search.description: Find and download Creative Commons sound effects via the Openverse API (Freesound, no key needed)

redub.description: Redub video with different voice (extract audio, transcribe, TTS, replace)
redub.usage: uv run tools/redub.py --input video.mp4 --voice-id VOICE_ID --output dubbed.mp4

options.stt-model: scribe_v2 (default). Deprecated ids are accepted with a warning: scribe_v1 (sent as is), scribe_v1_experimental (sent as scribe_v2)
options.model: eleven_multilingual_v2 (default), eleven_flash_v2_5, eleven_v3, eleven_v4 (also on --sync, with stability+similarity). Deprecated eleven_turbo_v2_5 is accepted with a warning and sent as eleven_flash_v2_5

addmusic.description: Add or generate background music, optionally duck it under speech and place timed sound effects with --events
addmusic.usage: uv run tools/addmusic.py -i video.mp4 -m music.wav --duck [--events effects.json] -o mixed.mp4

options.duck: Lower music during speech; --speech supplies isolated narration
options.events: JSON array of {path, atSeconds, gain}, relative paths from the JSON file
options.dry-run: Validate without writes or paid generation

dewatermark.description: Remove watermarks using AI inpainting (ProPainter) - supports local and RunPod cloud
dewatermark.usage: uv run tools/dewatermark.py --input video.mp4 --preset sora --output clean.mp4 --runpod
dewatermark.requires: Modal or RunPod account, OR local NVIDIA GPU + ProPainter (~2GB)

locate_watermark.description: Helper tool to identify watermark coordinates using grid overlay and verification

verify_setup.description: Verify toolkit setup - check prerequisites, optional components (Blender), cloud GPU, R2, and voice configuration

modal_setup.description: Deploy the Modal apps and write their endpoint URLs into .env (URLs read from Modal's API); --list shows deploy/.env status, --sync-env fixes .env without deploying, --hf-secret / HF_SECRET_NAME picks the Hugging Face secret for gated apps
modal_setup.requires: uv sync --extra modal, authenticated Modal CLI

notebooklm_brand.description: Post-process NotebookLM videos with custom branding (trim outro, add logo/URL)
notebooklm_brand.usage: uv run tools/notebooklm_brand.py --input video.mp4 --logo logo.png --url 'mysite.com' --output branded.mp4

cutdown.description: Social cut-downs to 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5, optional highlight segments and subject tracking; FFmpeg for all modes, optional vision extra for --mode track
cutdown.usage: uv run tools/cutdown.py --input input.mp4 --platform shorts [--mode blur|crop|pad|track] [--segment START-END[@FOCUS] ...]

options.platform: shorts, reels (9:16, 3 min), tiktok (9:16, 10 min), square (1:1), feed (4:5) - sets the default format and warns past the short-form limit
options.mode: blur (fit over a blurred copy, default), crop (fill, cut the sides; --focus 0-1), pad (fit over --pad-color or --brand bgDark); track follows a single face or --box subject, holding position on loss (uv sync --extra vision)
options.segments: --start/--end for one range, repeated --segment for a highlight reel joined with click-free audio fades; @FOCUS sets crop focus per segment
options.box: track mode: x,y,width,height in source pixels at each segment start; automatic single-face detection by default
options.max-pan-speed: Maximum source pixels per second, default 600

highlights.description: Select complete transcript sentences, keep the last repeated take, shorten pauses and render highlights; emit cutdown --segment arguments on the source timeline
highlights.usage: uv run tools/highlights.py --video input.mp4 --transcript words.json --output highlights.mp4 [--seconds 45] [--keep first|last] [--dry-run]

image_edit.description: AI image editing using Qwen-Image (Edit-2511 by default, Apache-2.0; 2.1 as a non-commercial Modal opt-in) - style transfer, backgrounds, prompts
image_edit.usage: uv run tools/image_edit.py --input photo.jpg --prompt 'Add sunglasses' --output edited.png
image_edit.backend: qwen-image-edit-2511 (default) / qwen-image-2.1 (IMAGE_EDIT_MODEL=qwen-image-2.1 at Modal deploy time)

upscale.description: AI image upscaling using RealESRGAN - 2x/4x with optional face enhancement

sadtalker.description: Generate talking head videos from portrait image + audio using SadTalker
sadtalker.usage: uv run tools/sadtalker.py --image portrait.png --audio voiceover.mp3 --preprocess full --output talking.mp4

soulx.description: Generate talking head videos from portrait image + audio using SoulX-FlashHead — holds identity across long renders and preserves the input aspect ratio (16:9 in, 16:9 out)
soulx.usage: uv run tools/soulx.py --image presenter_16x9.png --audio voiceover.mp3 --size 768 --output narrator.mp4

options.model: pro (default) or lite. Lite is for drafts only (tested on ~2.6s clips; long-take drift unmeasured): ~8x faster per chunk, no torch.compile, unloaded before any Pro render
options.size: target long edge, default 768; aspect ratio follows the input image
options.width/height: exact dimensions instead of size; multiples of 16 (Pro) or 32 (Lite, so 768x432 is illegal; 512x288 / 1024x576 are exact 16:9)
options.faceCrop: upstream face detect+crop, square-only so it discards a 16:9 framing, default off
options.compare: also write a labelled side-by-side against an existing render

soulx.estimatedCost: Pro ~$0.0024 per second of output (measured 6.4-7.9x realtime on A10G), plus a one-off ~600s torch.compile per container per resolution; Lite ~$0.0004 per second of output

qwen3_tts.description: Generate speech using Qwen3-TTS - built-in voices, emotion control, voice cloning

options.pacingQC: results include wpm + pacing label (fast/slow/ok); --max-wpm clamps fast takes with pitch-preserving atempo (floor 0.85x, --min-tempo lowers it to 0.7x)

sixtydb_tts.description: Generate speech using 60db cloud TTS - REST, streaming, and websocket transports

options.voice-id: 60db voice UUID (defaults to SIXTYDB_VOICE_ID or 60db default voice)
options.output-format: Audio format: mp3 (default), wav, ogg, flac (synthesize transport)

sync_timing.description: Sync scene durationSeconds in Remotion config with actual audio durations

qc.description: Pre-render QC — missing assets, narration vs scene length, wpm pacing, per-scene and render loudness (integrated LUFS / true peak against YouTube's -14 LUFS, -1 dBTP), the render's frames (still stretches over --max-still seconds, black gaps, empty first frame), and with --layout the text in the page (off canvas, clipped, under 2.6% of the short side, WCAG AA contrast; product UI under data-qc="product" listed apart). --fix normalises loudness; scene originals kept in .qc-backup/
qc.requires: ffmpeg + ffprobe; --layout also needs Node, playwright/ (npm install) and Chrome or Playwright Chromium

contact_sheet.description: Contact sheet of a rendered video: one settled frame before each scene cut (colour-aware detection, so same-lightness cuts are found), tiled into one PNG for the video-design critique; --at for chosen times, --count for even spacing

align_captions.description: Align hand-estimated cap() caption timings in sprint-config.ts to actual TTS audio — transcribes each scene with ElevenLabs Scribe, fuzzy-matches phrases to word timestamps, patches fromSec/durSec in --apply mode

options.model: scribe_v2 (default). Deprecated ids are accepted with a warning: scribe_v1 (sent as is), scribe_v1_experimental (sent as scribe_v2)

captions.description: Word-level <name>.captions.json beside each narration file for the <Captions> component. Transcribes with ElevenLabs Scribe or local whisper and aligns the scene's .txt script onto the timing, so captions spell names as written; --srt/--vtt export sibling subtitles at sentence/pause boundaries, including offline from existing caption JSON
captions.usage: uv run tools/captions.py projects/my-video/public/audio/scenes [--engine scribe|whisper] [--script FILE] [--json]
captions.requires: ElevenLabs API key (scribe) or `uv sync --extra whisper` (whisper)

options.engine: auto (default: scribe when ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is set, else whisper), scribe, whisper
options.script: Narration text to align to (default: sibling <name>.txt); --no-script burns the raw transcript
options.max-words: Upper bound per cue, 1-30, default 7; split at sentence ends and gaps over 0.6s

flux2.description: AI image generation and editing using FLUX.2 Klein (4B by default, Apache-2.0; 9B as a non-commercial Modal opt-in) - text-to-image, image editing, and scene presets
flux2.backend: flux2-klein-4b (default) / flux2-klein-9b (FLUX2_MODEL=klein-9b at Modal deploy time); flux2-small-decoder on Modal
flux2.requires: Modal or RunPod account (klein-9B also needs the huggingface-token secret)
flux2.estimatedCost: $0.01-0.03 per image warm; ~$0.06 including a Modal cold start

ideogram4.description: Ideogram 4 text-to-image via hosted v4 API — best-in-class in-image text rendering and exact color/layout control through structured JSON captions
ideogram4.backend: ideogram-4 hosted v4 API (default); ideogram-4-5 hosted v2 API (--model 4.5 opt-in)
ideogram4.note: Commercial license via paid API. Skill `.claude/skills/ideogram4/` teaches the JSON caption format; Claude is the magic-prompt expander. Live-tested on --model 4, the default (json_prompt + text_prompt paths). --model 4.5 (opt-in) posts multipart to /v2/image/generate/ideogram-4-5: --speed maps to quality (FLASH and TURBO -> low, DEFAULT -> medium, QUALITY -> high) and --resolution must be auto or WxH (multiples of 32, sides >= 256, <= 2048x2048 pixels, aspect <= 6:1). Run live 2026-10-12: JSON captions render near-perfect text, plain prompts gain garbled filler text. 4.0 stays the default because 1280x720 is off 4.5's 32-pixel grid.

ltx2.description: AI video generation using LTX-2.3 22B (LTX-2.5 as a Modal deploy-time opt-in) - text-to-video, image-to-video clips with synchronized audio
ltx2.usage: uv run tools/ltx2.py --prompt "A sunset over the ocean" --output sunset.mp4
ltx2.backend: ltx-2.3-22b (default) / ltx-2.5-22b (LTX2_VERSION=2.5 at Modal deploy time)
ltx2.requires: Modal account, huggingface-token Modal secret whose account can download the gated weights: Google's Gemma 3 text encoder for 2.3 (approved by hand), Lightricks/LTX-2.5 for the opt-in (accept its terms)
ltx2.estimatedCost: ~$0.07 warm / ~$0.12 cold per 5s clip (LTX-2.3); ~$0.09-0.10 warm / ~$0.16 cold (LTX-2.5 opt-in). Measured 2026-10-12, GPU time at $2.50/h
ltx2.note: LTX-2.5 is an opt-in. Benchmarked against 2.3 on 2026-10-12 (docs/ltx2.md): 25-45% slower per clip, and the crt-terminal preset does not keep its look on 2.5. Responses carry a model field, printed as Model:.

ltx_extend.description: Lengthen an LTX image-to-video clip by continuing it from one of its own frames (the last good one) and joining the two with a short cross-fade; chains with --times. For shots longer than a ~5 s clip, instead of holding (reads as a pause) or ping-ponging (reads as a loop)
ltx_extend.requires: ltx2.py on Modal (each extension is one LTX clip, ~$0.08)

sync_check.description: Sound-to-picture sync for effects laid over generated footage: --clip says where in a clip to start a sound so its peak lands on the movement (prevention); --video/--cues measures the offset in a render and exits 1 past 0.1 s (validation). Kinds: peak (a sneeze, a jingle) and impact (where a movement stops)
sync_check.usage: uv run tools/sync_check.py --clip clip.mp4 --sfx sneeze.mp3 --window 2.5:4.5  |  uv run tools/sync_check.py --video out/video.mp4 --cues sync-cues.json

chain_video.description: Chain LTX-2 clips with visual continuity — each scene uses the last frame of the previous as input
chain_video.usage: uv run tools/chain_video.py --scenes-dir images/ --output-dir videos/ --prompt "Cinematic flow"
chain_video.backend: ltx-2.3-22b, or ltx-2.5-22b on an LTX2_VERSION=2.5 deployment (via ltx2.py)
chain_video.estimatedCost: ~$0.07-0.12 per scene on LTX-2.3 (delegates to ltx2)

youtube_upload.description: Upload a rendered video to YouTube via the Data API v3 (OAuth 2.0, resumable upload) — title/description/tags/thumbnail/captions/playlist, private/unlisted/public or scheduled publish
youtube_upload.backend: YouTube Data API v3 (OAuth 2.0 installed-app flow)
youtube_upload.requires: Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app); YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRETS_FILE

options.auth: --auth (interactive login, caches a refresh token per --account)
options.check: --check (read-only: channel, scopes, Data/Analytics API on or off, with the fix for each)

youtube_upload.note: Uploads require OAuth, not an API key. Default quota 10,000 units/day; videos.insert ~1600 units (~6 uploads/day). Unverified OAuth apps force uploads to private until Google-verified. Cached tokens live in _internal/.youtube/ (gitignored).

publish_kit.description: Subtitles and chapters for YouTube from a finished render: the render's audio transcribed once and aligned to the scene scripts gives one whole-video SRT and a chapter at each scene's cut, under YouTube's chapter rules
publish_kit.backend: ElevenLabs Scribe ($0.40/audio hour) or local whisper

options.fresh: --fresh (transcribe again; otherwise a saved transcript newer than the render is reused)

publish_kit.note: Writes out/publish/ (video.srt, video.captions.json, chapters.txt, kit.json). Chapter titles from project.json scenes[].title or the scene file names. /publish runs it before the dry run.

youtube_stats.description: How the channel's videos are doing: views, likes, comments per video and subscribers (Data API v3), plus watch time, retention, traffic sources and (if the API allows) impressions/CTR when the token has the YouTube Analytics scope; snapshots per run give deltas over time; --github adds the repo's traffic referrers
youtube_stats.backend: YouTube Data API v3 + YouTube Analytics API v2 (reuses youtube_upload.py's cached token)
youtube_stats.requires: a token from youtube_upload.py --auth; Analytics needs the API enabled and youtube_stats.py --auth
youtube_stats.note: Read-only. Snapshots go to _internal/.youtube/stats/<account>/ (gitignored). Analytics lags 1-2 days.

copy_lint.description: The first filter on anything public: refuses dashes and stock AI or marketing phrasing in files (HTML, Markdown, text, read as prose), strings, a branch's added lines (--diff) or commit subjects (--commits); the same rules gate video jobs, youtube_upload.py and voiceover.py
copy_lint.usage: uv run tools/copy_lint.py site/*.html --text "Title" | --diff origin/main --commits origin/main
copy_lint.note: Stdlib only. CI: .github/workflows/copy-lint.yml lints each PR's new lines and commit subjects. Includes taste-skill's stock marketing phrases.

voice_prosody.description: Measure pitch spread (F0 semitone sd, p5-p95) of any audio, and write a livelier clone reference: pitch contour expanded around the median and slowed (Praat PSOLA). A clone copies its reference's pace and intonation, so fix the clip rather than stretching the output
voice_prosody.usage: uv run tools/voice_prosody.py measure FILES... [--json]; uv run tools/voice_prosody.py expand IN.wav OUT.wav [--pitch 2.0] [--tempo 0.85]

options.pitch: exponent on pitch deviations around the median (1 = unchanged; 1.7-2.2 useful)
options.tempo: speed factor for the reference (0.85 = 15% slower)

voice_prosody.guide: narration: sd under ~2 st sounds flat, 3-4 st normal, over ~5 theatrical

pick_takes.description: Choose the best take per phrase from several voiceover runs: score = pitch spread minus a pace penalty outside 140-170 wpm; copies winners (+ .txt) to the output, slows only a winner over --max-wpm, never below --min-tempo; --json writes takes.json with every candidate

pick_music.description: Recommend one of several music takes (music_gen.py --variations N) with its reasons, for a person to confirm: rules out takes shorter than the video, clipping or with a mid-track dropout; scores calm under voice/text (onsets a second), movement (loudness spread), the ending (a fade, or a cut-off the video's own fade must cover) and whether a note or a level change lands on each act cut. Measured, not heard: commands show the recommendation and ask the user to listen; video_job-style agents take it and record why
pick_music.usage: uv run tools/pick_music.py public/audio/music_*.mp3 --target 44.5 --cuts 11.5,17.5,37.5 --under text --fade-out 1.5 [--pick public/audio/music.mp3] [--json]

options.target: the video's length in seconds; a shorter take is ruled out
options.cuts: comma-separated seconds of the video's turns
options.under: voice | text | none: what the music sits under (voice and text prefer a calm bed)
options.fade-out: seconds of music fade the video applies, so a take still playing at the end isn't penalised
options.pick: copy the recommended take to this path

audition.description: Put each music take under the finished picture for the user to watch and choose: one render serves every take, each mixed in with ffmpeg in seconds at the composition's volume and fades, trimmed to the video and normalised to -14 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP. Keeps the video's own audio (narration) unless --drop-audio; --recommend adds pick_music.py's measured pick and flags a tie the measures can't separate
audition.usage: uv run tools/audition.py --video out/video.nomusic.mp4 --music public/audio/bg_*.mp3 --volume 0.15 --fade-out 1.5 [--drop-audio] [--recommend --cuts 12,31,50 --under voice] [--json]

options.volume: music gain, as in the composition
options.start / fade-in / fade-out: where the music starts and its fades, seconds
options.drop-audio: discard the render's own audio (an old music bed)

video_job.description: Async video jobs for agents: a scene spec (or a brief via VIDEO_JOB_EXPANDER) in, a QC-checked MP4 out. submit returns in seconds with a job id and estimate; a detached worker runs voiceover -> visuals (Ideogram/LTX/FLUX) -> captions -> build (concept-explainer-short, 9:16 or 16:9) -> qc --fix -> publish (R2 URL when configured). State on disk under jobs/<id>/, one job at a time, --max-usd refused before any spend and enforced before each paid step, receipts as JSON lines in MEDIA_SPEND_LOG (or the agent workspace's logs/ when VIDEO_JOB_WORKSPACE is set). catalog lists what the toolkit makes, from this registry. Failed or cancelled jobs resume from their first missing output; status has timestamped events, warnings and a per-host ETA; renders are encoded under 9.5 MB for chat attachments; catalog/presets report what this host can make (host), and submit refuses a provider it has no key or endpoint for (unavailable) before any spend; kits (kits/<name>/kit.json in the agent workspace or the toolkit: brand, voice, format, own photos) fill a spec, file scenes use a person's own photos or clips, and text scenes get a local brand-colour background on a host without FLUX
video_job.usage: uv run tools/video_job.py submit --spec spec.json --max-usd 1.00 --json; then status JOB_ID --json; result JOB_ID --json

options.brief: One-paragraph description; needs VIDEO_JOB_EXPANDER to submit (estimate answers with a skeleton without one)
options.spec: Finished spec JSON file or '-' (scenes with text + visual kind/prompt); the agent-is-the-LLM path
options.max-usd: Refuse when the estimate is above this (default 2.00, env VIDEO_JOB_MAX_USD); worker stops before the next paid step at the cap; resume --max-usd raises a stopped job's cap
options.keep: prune: newest jobs never pruned (default 10; submit auto-prunes with VIDEO_JOB_KEEP)
options.older-than: prune: only jobs finished at least this many days ago

video_job.prices: PRICES table in the module (presets --json prints it), checked against receipts 2026-11-01: ltx clip 0.10, ideogram image 0.03/0.06/0.10 by speed, flux image 0.0075, qwen3 voice 0.01/scene (actuals booked from the Modal cost event), elevenlabs 0.20/1k chars, scribe captions 0.40/audio hour

exitCodes.2: refused or not ready (budget_exceeded, no_expander, job not done)

blender_render.description: Shot spec in, Blender film or clips out: builds a 3D scene from a JSON spec (a rigged cartoon cast described as build, face, hair, clothes and a seed; a desk set, or a studio stage with a phone, a card or an imported model; shots by type; acting beats in seconds or on narration words), checks every camera by geometry (subject in frame, nothing blocking, a moving lens clear of the cast) with a solver that moves failing cameras, writes a labelled contact sheet, then renders the film with sound placed on the keyed motion, or one clip per shot (MP4, or transparent WebM if asked) with a clips.json manifest, for Remotion's BlenderClip, a moviepy build, a video job's file scene or an editor
blender_render.usage: uv run tools/blender_render.py check spec.json && uv run tools/blender_render.py render spec.json [--clips --alpha --to projects/NAME/public/blender]

options.doctor: Find Blender, ffmpeg and Pillow, and time a test render on this machine (s/frame and minutes for the spec)
options.check: Build, verify shots, measure exposure, write stills + contact_sheet.png (exit 1 on a failed check, 2 on a spec error)
options.render: Check, then render the film with sound
options.open: Open the built scene.blend in Blender to look round it
options.--clips: One clip per shot in out/clips/ with clips.json and each shot's effects as a WAV, instead of one film
options.--alpha: Transparent background: clips are WebM (VP9 with alpha)
options.--prores: Also ProRes 4444 .mov per clip, for other editors
options.--shots: Comma-separated shot ids to check or render
options.--to: Copy the clips and manifest into a project's public/ folder
options.--force: Render even if a check failed

env.BLENDER: Path to the Blender binary if not on PATH or in the usual install folder

DataChart.description: LineChart (one line or several series with a legend), BarChart, Counter and SplitBar drawn as SVG frame by frame: brand-themed (chartTheme, dark or light), a line that draws to narration keyframes with a y axis that grows with the data, cue-timed bands, bar highlights (own colour per bar), counters and split-bar labels. Labels are real text, so qc.py --layout checks them

PageTurns.description: One scene that turns into new pages in place, each on its narration cue: a hard edge sweeps across with the next page behind it (no fade). For showing the same thing again in a new way (one chart in three design sources, before and after a fix). Between scenes use @remotion/transitions wipe()

MazeDecoration.description: Animated isometric grid decoration for video corners with wave animation

FilmGrain.description: SVG noise overlay for cinematic film texture

Terminal.description: Terminal window that types commands and prints output (ok, error, dim), plus select menus, each line on a narration cue; scrolls once full, blinking prompt at the end. terminalTheme(brand) reads a brand's colors.terminal block; typedUntil() gives the frame a command finishes typing. For CLI and Claude Code demos, nothing screen-recorded

BlenderClip.description: Plays a Blender render as an element of a Remotion scene: one clip per shot from tools/blender_render.py --clips (transparent with --alpha), played once then held, with the shot's own sound effects. blenderClip(manifest, id) reads clips.json and gives the clip's length and event('alert') frames, so captions and cuts land on the acting. Throws if the spec's fps isn't the composition's

LivingPhoto.description: An image-to-video clip of a person (ltx2.py --input) that plays forward once and holds its last good frame with a slow push-in; hold/trim cut around a late stranger or an early glitch, fit slows a slightly short clip to its shot (to 0.8x). Never plays backwards; lengthen with ltx_extend.py
